rates.explainer: Treasury yields are the interest rate the US government pays to borrow. The 2-year follows what traders expect the Fed to do with rates; the 10-year reflects longer-run growth and inflation. Rising yields usually weigh on Nasdaq stocks, because the future profits that tech prices depend on are worth less today when safe bonds pay more. Falling yields usually help.

draft.headline: Durable goods figures not in our feed; NQ barely moved
draft.summary: The durable goods report landed at 08:30 ET, but the actual figures are not in our data, so we cannot say whether it beat or missed forecasts. NQ slipped 0.08% in the measured window while yields edged up.
draft.what_it_means: Durable goods orders track demand for long-lasting items like machines and planes, and they hint at business investment. Forecasts were 2.0% headline and 0.6% core, up from 0.0% and 0.3% previously, so economists expected a rebound. But the actual numbers are not reported here, so there is no verdict yet on the economy or the Fed. A stronger print would suggest firm investment; a weak one would point to caution. It is simply not known.
draft.market_reaction: In the window from 08:29 to 08:45 ET, Nasdaq 100 futures fell 0.08% and S&P 500 futures fell 0.07%. The VIX fear gauge rose 0.34% and the dollar was basically unchanged at +0.02%. Earlier in the session NQ was up 0.41% at 29,556.50. These are small moves, and futures prices are about 10 minutes delayed.
draft.rates_read: The 2-year yield, which tracks Fed expectations, rose 1.0bp in the window to 4.728% and is up 1.7bp today. The 10-year rose 1.3bp to 4.991%, near 5%, and is up 0.5bp today. Over the past week both fell, the 10-year by 12.0bp. Yields this high tend to weigh on Nasdaq stocks, since future tech profits are worth less today.

draft.learn: "Core" durable goods orders strip out transportation, mainly aircraft, which swing wildly order to order. The core figure is the cleaner read on underlying business investment, while the headline number can jump on a single large plane order.
